note: The closest thing to a core fit in this batch, and the only miss is a criterion that was never tested. He clears income decisively — $6,000 paid in full on a credit card during the call with no price objection, no budget anchor and no request for instalments. He is a textbook good-to-great case: a former national-qualifier bodybuilder at 18-19% body fat naming 12% as the target he used to hold, which is the exact 'still good, wants great' shape the stated ICP describes. Not deconditioned is unambiguous — 15 to 20 years of training, military conditioning, back in the gym two days after finishing treatment. Neglected_health is recorded as a match because the thing he is buying to fix is a five-to-six-year slide caused by children and COVID, which is precisely neglect; the acute infection is a separate and recent event rather than the reason he is on the call. 'Successful' is a miss only because nothing establishes it: he is a military veteran who says he works in the fitness industry, and the rep never asked what he actually does. Two observations worth carrying up. First, this reinforces the existing finding that income screening measures the wrong thing — the buyer who paid full price fastest is the one whose occupation was never established. Second, and more important, a prospect can score four out of five on the stated ICP while being, on the day of sale, one week clear of a PICC line and three weeks from finishing heavy antibiotics. The criteria have no clinical dimension whatsoever, and this call is the sharpest illustration of that in the corpus.
